summary: Cross-model gap analysis of the hipfire autoresearch machinery (Claude finds, Codex refutes)

result.summary: Three themes dominate. (1) The new two-arm serve_harness gate is measuring the wrong things at the wrong precision: perf is read on the FP32-deterministic parity path (or a wall-inclusive CLI number with the GPU-only kernel_decode_tok_s dropped over HTTP), while the production-Q8 sampled-coherence arm is declared "reproducible in one seeded run" even though Q8 stochastic rounding and post-first-divergence trajectory drift make single-seed variant-vs-baseline comparison unsound and low-power. (2) The redesign that exists to kill the greedy single-prompt crutch has not been wired into the highest-stakes decision — rollover composite promotion still runs the temp-0 unique-ratio crutch — and the self-stopping loop is broken: the K-stop counts only DEAD/INCONCLUSIVE, so coherence/parity failures loop forever, INCONCLUSIVE near-wins are abandoned as if dead, and the coherence arm has no semantic/value validator so fluent-but-wrong output passes both arms. (3) The strategic "kernel tuning is tapped" verdict is an artifact of the machinery's own scope — a single-kernel value-preserving operator blind to fusion/launch-gap, a wall_pct-only selector that ignores the project's already-validated occupancy/compiler-schedulability headroom predictors, an end-to-end tok/s discriminator below its own noise floor, and a batch-1 short-context-only census — so "tapped" describes the instrument, not the search space.

gaps.title: ARM B's single-seed subset test is unsound: seed fixes token selection, not the Q8 logit vector, and a numerically-different variant diverges trajectory after the first differing logit
gaps.gap: The determinism matrix claims threading GenerateRequest.seed into the sampler RNG makes ARM B (temp 1.0, production Q8) 'apples-to-apples in ONE run each.' Two independent mechanisms break this on the exact a3b model under test. (a) The seed only fixes token SELECTION given a logit vector; it does not fix the logit vector — Q8 DeltaNet stochastic rounding (multi-GPU / EF-disabled paths) plus nondeterministic FP-atomic reduction order are separate, unseeded entropy sources, so two same-seed ARM-B runs differ by run-to-run rounding noise (the project's own rule: Q8 makes even greedy non-reproducible). (b) Even if rounding were seeded, a WIN kernel is by construction numerically different; at temp 1.0 a token is a step function of the CDF, so the first position where variant and baseline logits differ picks a different token and the trajectories diverge into completely different sequences thereafter. A shared seed buys per-run reproducibility, NOT variant-vs-baseline comparability. Compounding this, the choice of one seed conflated reproducibility (an estimator property) with detection power (a sample-size property): attractor onset is a rare Bernoulli event (the gfx1151 case was 1-of-5 prompts), so a variant raising attractor probability ~2%→~20% still passes ~80% of single seeds. Note serve_harness.py has no --seed arg at all today, so ARM B is currently fully unseeded.
gaps.suggestion: Drop the single-seed subset premise. Run ARM B over a fixed seed-SET (8-16 seeds), the SAME set paired for base and variant, and compare attractor/runaway RATES with a proportion test against the baseline's own rate as null — this is the only sound way to attribute a temp-1.0 coherence delta to the kernel rather than to trajectory divergence or rounding noise. Bank the offending prompt+seed into the per-arch guard set. Before trusting any delta, empirically verify baseline-vs-baseline at a fixed seed reproduces (it will not on stochastic Q8/multi-GPU); if you insist on a single-run design, seed the Q8 rounding RNG and confirm reductions are order-stable first. The fallback 'seeded-Q8 text-exact' parity is broken for the same reason and will false-PARITY_FAIL baseline against itself.

gaps.title: The composite/rollover promotion gate — the highest-stakes measurement in the system — still runs the exact greedy single-prompt crutch the redesign exists to kill, so cross-kernel joint attractors slip through
gaps.gap: Both live rollover paths validate composite coherence with the biased greedy path: rollover_stack.sh and rollover_v2.sh (v2 and v3-queue) measure baseline and stack with ONE hardcoded temp-0 prompt and a len>15 / unique-ratio>0.35 word check. The review proves this path structurally hides attractors (argmax is maximally predictable) and records the promoted gfx1151 stack passing exactly this greedy check yet throwing a repetition attractor on the prose turn at temp 1.0. The spec claims rollover judges the composite with ARM A (perf) + ARM B (coherence on the guard set), but ARM B is not implemented in either rollover script — the code still runs the crutch, and none of the rollover paths call serve_harness.py or the guard-prompt set. This matters most precisely for the best-per-kernel merge: two individually-coherent wins can jointly attract (register/LDS/phase interaction), and that emergent attractor is a temp-1.0 sampled phenomenon a single greedy unique-ratio prompt cannot surface. The one validation supposed to catch cross-kernel negative interaction before advancing the baseline runs on the axis blind to it.
gaps.suggestion: Wire the two-arm serve_harness gate into rollover BEFORE it is used as a promotion judge. ARM B (sampled temp-1.0, seed-SET, multiturn chain over the genre battery + the full coherence_prompts_<arch> guard set) must run on the composite, not a single greedy prompt. Until that exists, treat every rollover promotion as unvalidated and do not advance B_a on the greedy check alone.

gaps.title: Perf delta is read from ARM A (FP32-deterministic) — the wrong kernel, wrong reduction order, and wrong occupancy regime — so a Q8 variant can show delta=0 by construction
gaps.gap: The design measures perf inside ARM A, which runs under HIPFIRE_DETERMINISTIC=1 + FP32 DeltaNet — not production. (1) It runs gated_delta_net_f32 instead of _q8_fast, so a Q8-DeltaNet variant shows delta=0 by construction. (2) HIPFIRE_DETERMINISTIC forces the k2 single-block K reduction in GEMM (gemm.rs:13713), changing the reduction kernel's occupancy/VGPR/latency vs the production multi-block path — a GEMV/GEMM variant's measured speedup is on a serialized reduction production never uses. (3) FP32 state has different byte traffic and register pressure, shifting the very memory-latency/occupancy regime the BOD says decode is bound by. A variant can win at FP32-det and lose at Q8, or vice versa.
gaps.suggestion: Decouple the three measurements onto the right serves: keep PARITY on the FP32-det serve (ARM A); measure PERF on the production Q8 serve using a repeated fixed warmed prompt with adaptive MWU (as the deprecated ab_certify_v2p did); run COHERENCE on the production Q8 serve. Never read a perf number from the determinism arm. The perf delta and coherence check share the Q8 serve; only parity uses FP32-det.

gaps.title: The perf instrument regressed from adaptive MWU-on-one-warmed-prompt to a single sequential 5-genre battery run: wall-inclusive, JIT/shape-contaminated, no interleave, no clock-VOID, and the GPU-only counter is dropped over HTTP
gaps.gap: serve_harness reads timings.decode_tok_s (daemon decode-window wall) or estimates (dtoks-1)/(wall-ttft) (fully wall-inclusive, HTTP/stream overhead) and averages every numeric decode value across 5 HETEROGENEOUS single-shot genre prompts — including decode_estimated values mixed with reported ones. The daemon computes kernel_decode_tok_s (daemon.rs:9490-9534, DFlash 4212-4267) but buildTimings (cli/index.ts:3568-3573) omits it, so the GPU-only counter is unobservable over HTTP; the multi-GPU AR done envelope (daemon.rs:6802) doesn't even compute it. Host overhead H is roughly additive per token, compressing a true GPU-only X% kernel win to ~X·t_gpu/(t_gpu+H) below the floor the loop chases → false DEADs on real small wins. The battery runs 5 different-shape prompts once each with only a 'Hi'/max_tokens=1 prewarm, so each shape JITs cold (3-7x slow, per the project's per-shape JIT rule) and the median conflates cross-workload variance with measurement noise — cannot resolve a 2% win against the ±1-3% band. The design also runs baseline serve fully then variant serve fully (sequential block design maximally exposed to thermal/DPM drift) and captures NO clock state (no pp_dpm_sclk), on the contended 4×gfx1201 box where busy-sysfs silently under-clocks ~13%. This is a triple regression vs the deprecated ab_certify_v2p (2 warmups before a fixed measured prompt, kernel_decode_tok_s preference, adaptive 4-16 round MWU, >4% clock-skew VOID).
gaps.suggestion: Forward kernel_decode_tok_s over HTTP on the AR path and gate the perf delta on THAT GPU-only counter; use the CLI/text path for behavior/coherence only. Restore the dropped guardrails: interleave N repeated A/B measures of the SAME fixed warmed prompt and resolve with an MWU/dominance stat + fixed noise-margin (not a 5-genre median); add a throwaway warmup pass per measured shape; capture pp_dpm_sclk before/after each arm and VOID on >~4% drift; refuse to compare a reported decode_tok_s against an estimated one (require the same method on both sides); and record the prompt md5 in the ledger.

gaps.title: The K-stop rule counts only DEAD/INCONCLUSIVE — COHERENCE_FAIL, PARITY_FAIL, VOID, LOSS/NOISE never increment exhaustion — so a kernel whose failures are coherence/parity loops forever, and the driver's counter diverges from the supervisor's
gaps.gap: ab_certify_v2.sh emits WIN/DEAD/INCONCLUSIVE/COHERENCE_FAIL/VOID/BUILD_FAIL, but update_exhaustion.py counts only v in ('DEAD','INCONCLUSIVE') (WIN resets, everything else silent no-op); check_exhausted.py stops only when every BOD candidate hits K. So a kernel where Codex keeps writing value-changing edits (repeated COHERENCE_FAIL, or PARITY_FAIL in the new arm — which ab_certify_v2p exits before even ledgering) never accumulates exhaustion → K=5 never fires → the driver burns codex rounds on it forever. The two-arm redesign multiplies this by making coherence/parity first-class rejection axes invisible to the stop rule. Separately, the supervisor keeps an independent counter — hipfire_ar.py DEAD_VERDICTS={DEAD,INCONCLUSIVE,LOSS,NOISE} recomputed as a DB tail-streak — while the driver counts only DEAD/INCONCLUSIVE by round-prefix from the ledger; the certify bounds-gate (DB streak) and the driver stop (exhaustion_<arch>.json) can disagree, so the gate can REFUSE (exit 3) a kernel the driver still schedules (wasting the round) or vice-versa. A prior WIN can also keep the supervisor from ever declaring exhaustion even after later dead streaks.
gaps.suggestion: Unify ONE exhaustion definition and count every non-WIN terminal verdict meaning 'this lever did not help' — COHERENCE_FAIL and repeated PARITY_FAIL must increment (a kernel only made fast by breaking coherence/value IS exhausted for the loop). Keep BUILD_FAIL/VOID as retryable-infra but add a separate per-kernel infra-fail cap so an un-buildable variant can't spin. Make hipfire_ar.py READ the same exhaustion_<arch>.json the driver writes instead of recomputing from the DB, so the gate and stop can never diverge.

gaps.title: The coherence arm detects only structural repetition — no semantic-correctness or instruction-following check — so a Q8-timing-specific value-corrupting-but-fluent kernel passes both arms
gaps.gap: The parity gate's own motivating failure is 'a kernel that drops half its output rows but still reads fluently.' ARM A catches that only if it reproduces in the FP32+HIPFIRE_DETERMINISTIC path; a corruption manifesting only under production-Q8 timing (an occupancy/race effect the FP32-det path serializes away) passes ARM A. ARM B is then the sole line of defense at Q8 — but ARM B checks ONLY unique-token-ratio, max-token-frequency, 3-gram density, runaway (finish==length) and empty (send(), lines 241-254). It has NO semantic or instruction-following check: the reason prompt's final number is never verified, code is never compiled/run, the 'exactly three sentences' / 'exactly five numbered tips' constraints are unchecked, and tool_calls are captured (line 231) but never validated for JSON well-formedness (which coherence_probe flags and serve_harness does not). A kernel yielding fluent-but-wrong math, dropped list items, or malformed tool-calls is COHERENT to this gate. The top-level ab_certify_v2.sh only greps runaway/empty/attractor/error/panic, so all of these pass.
gaps.suggestion: Add cheap per-genre validators to ARM B: number-match on the reason prompt, sentence-count==3 on factual, numbered-line count==5 on instruct, py_compile on code output, json.loads validity on any tool_calls. Treat any validator failure the variant introduces that the baseline didn't as COHERENCE_FAIL, same as an attractor. Also run one ARM-B check at temp 0 through the PRODUCTION Q8 path (not FP32-det) so a Q8-only value corruption has a place to surface that ARM A structurally cannot.

gaps.title: 'Fix the offending kernel while keeping perf' is structurally impossible for the barrier/sync-removal win class — the only fresh-process-surviving win found — because the removed synchronization IS the speedup; and ablation localization is ill-defined for joint attractors
gaps.gap: The review states the sole fresh-process-surviving win (gfx1151 +3.07%) came from LDS-barrier / shared-memory-staging removal on catastrophically under-occupied kernels (attention ~1.4% occ, rmsnorm ~0.4%). Barrier/staging removal is a canonical source of read-before-write / cross-wave races — the very synchronization removed to gain speed is what its absence turns into a temp-1.0 attractor. So for this win-class, 'fix the coherence bug while preserving the perf win' means 're-add correctness without re-adding the barrier cost,' which is often impossible: perf is causally tied to the bug. The spec makes correct-and-keep-perf the PRIMARY fixer path and ablate-re-open the fallback — the evidence inverts that expected rate for the most productive win-class. Second defect: the fixer localizes the culprit by stack-minus-one ablation, which assumes a single buggy kernel; if the attractor is an interaction (two individually-coherent wins that jointly attract), stack-minus-one shows removing EITHER fixes it → it reports two different 'culprits' by drop order, and 'fix that kernel's bug' is undefined because neither kernel is individually buggy. (Note: no fixer is implemented in the checked-in code yet — this is a design gap, not a bug in an existing fixer.)
gaps.suggestion: Default the fixer to ablate-and-re-open for any win whose lever is barrier/sync/LDS-staging removal (detect from the lever tag); reserve correct-and-keep-perf for wins where perf and correctness are separable (instruction-selection, tiling that didn't touch synchronization). Budget the fixer as ablate-FIRST with correct-and-keep as opportunistic best-effort. For localization, replace stack-minus-one with a leave-one-in / add-one-at-a-time sweep against the original baseline to detect interaction, and when two kernels jointly attract, re-open BOTH kernels' search and mark the pair as an interaction constraint the loop must respect.

gaps.title: 'Kernel tuning is tapped' is an artifact of a single-kernel value-preserving search operator plus a BOD census blind to launch and inter-kernel gap time — the dominant batch-1 latency lever (fusion/hipGraph) is structurally invisible to both
gaps.gap: The '~0% fresh-process' verdict is the OUTPUT of a search whose operator is 'Codex writes a value-preserving variant of ONE hot kernel.' That operator can never propose the levers that matter most in a latency-bound regime: kernel FUSION (fewer launches / fewer HBM round-trips for intermediates), persistent/megakernels, or hipGraph-scope changes — all of which cross the kernel boundary the operator preserves. The BOD reinforces the blindness: it measures per-kernel wall_pct/L2/occ/vgpr/lds but has NO counter for launch overhead or inter-kernel host/dispatch GAP time, a first-order term for batch-1 decode with hundreds of tiny kernels. The project's own history confirms the lever lives outside the loop: the two largest recent batch-1 gains — hipGraph re-capture (+6.4% graded-MoE decode #464; the gfx12 99→50 tok/s replay fix; and the documented 101→126.6 tok/s daemon hipGraph) — are structural/cross-kernel, found OUTSIDE driver_v3, and would score zero in a per-kernel A/B. So 'tapped' is evidence only that intra-kernel edits are tapped.
gaps.suggestion: Read the null result as 'the operator and census are mis-scoped for latency-bound batch-1,' not 'kernels are done.' (1) Add an inter-kernel gap/launch-overhead row to the BOD (total decode wall minus sum(kernel wall) = dispatch+host shadow); if >5-10%, fusion/hipGraph is a bigger lever than any single-kernel edit. (2) Add a second search operator that proposes fusion of adjacent BOD kernels (rmsnorm+residual+quant, gate_up+top-k) and hipGraph-scope changes, certified by the SAME two-arm gate. Repoint the loop before abandoning kernels.

gaps.title: The headroom predictor the doc asks for already exists — twice — in the project's own validated findings, but the candidate gate (wall_pct >= 3%) ignores both, so rounds burn on compiler-saturated hot kernels
gaps.gap: Q5b asks for a principled tunable-vs-compiler-saturated predictor; the project has already empirically derived two, and neither is encoded in the BOD or the fewest-attempts-over-all-wall%>=3% selection policy (hotness only). P1 (occupancy shadow-price): the gfx1151 +3.07% came from removing LDS staging + barriers on catastrophically under-occupied kernels (attention 1.4%, rmsnorm 0.4% occ) — on batch-1 latency-bound decode, occupancy is the binding constraint and headroom = occupancy-deficit × a removable occupancy tax (LDS/barriers/spill exposed because too few waves hide them). P2 (compiler-schedulability, committed 2026-07-04): the attention register-ring win found the compiler AUTO-pipelines simple gathers (rmsnorm/residual prefetch = DEAD no-ops) but NOT __shfl_xor-serialized reduction loops — 'manual wins ONLY there.' Both point at the same static feature class (barrier/shuffle/serialized-reduction kernels). A plain quantized GEMV has neither property → correctly predicted saturated, yet the gate gives it the same 5-attempt budget as an occupancy-starved barrier kernel. (Codex verification was incomplete on this item — treat the mechanism as asserted-plausible.)
gaps.suggestion: Encode P1 and P2 as static+dynamic BOD features per kernel: has_lds / has_barrier / has_crosslane_shuffle / spill (from the .hsaco via the gfx-kernel-metadata skill) and occupancy-vs-latency-hiding-threshold. Compute headroom = f(occupancy_deficit × removable_tax, non_schedulable_loops), then (a) DESELECT hot-but-saturated kernels (high wall%, moderate occ, no barrier/shuffle, no spill) from the candidate set, and (b) budget attempts proportional to headroom rather than fewest-attempts-uniform. This flags gfx1151's attention/rmsnorm and skips the simple-gather GEMVs the loop burned rounds on.

gaps.title: FP32 value-preservation does not imply Q8 value-preservation for reassociation-class changes — the dominant lever type — and HIPFIRE_DETERMINISTIC actively pins the one variable the variant is changing
gaps.gap: The design asserts 'parity need not run at production precision,' but the largest lever class the loop tries (row-tiling, reduction-tree restructuring, register-ring prefetch that reorders accumulation, k-split changes) is reassociation of floating-point sums. FP32's 24-bit mantissa absorbs reassociation that is a no-op there yet shifts the rounding boundary under Q8's far coarser quantization, flipping argmax more often. Worse, HIPFIRE_DETERMINISTIC forces a single canonical reduction order (gemm.rs:13713 k2), so the parity arm actively PINS the one variable — reduction order — the variant is changing, guaranteeing FP32-det parity is blind to it. Per the project's own '5% attention error cascades into an attractor within ~10 tokens' rule, a reassociation that only bites under Q8 rounding is exactly an attractor generator ARM A cannot see and single-seed ARM B usually misses. (The current ab_certify_v2p does have a narrow Q8 token-id parity check on one temp-0 prompt; the redesign moves parity to FP32-det and loses even that.)
gaps.suggestion: For any variant that changes accumulation/reduction structure, add a Q8-precision value check that is tolerance-based rather than bit-exact: run base and variant on the Q8 path and compare per-position top-k logit overlap or symmetric KLD against a small threshold over a fixed prompt. This catches Q8-only argmax drift that both text-exact-FP32 parity and single-seed coherence let through.

gaps.title: L2-hit% is the wrong lever-class discriminator and wall_pct the wrong candidate priority for latency-bound batch-1 decode — the loop found its one surviving win despite the discriminator, not because of it
gaps.gap: The BOD derives bound_class from a single binary L2-hit threshold (DRAM-thrash <40%, cache-resident >60%). L2-hit% measures WHERE bytes come from, not WHAT the kernel stalls on. In batch-1 decode — which the findings call latency-limited, running 'in the shadow of memory latency' — a kernel can be >60% L2-resident yet stalled on L2 round-trip LATENCY, not DRAM bandwidth and not ALU. Two kernels both at 70% L2-hit need opposite levers (ALU-bound wants instruction-selection; latency-bound wants prefetch/more in-flight/higher occupancy), and L2-hit% cannot separate them — so it mis-assigns lever class. The ONE fresh-surviving win (gfx1151 +3.07%) came from a LATENCY lever (removing LDS barriers on 1.4%-occupancy kernels) the L2-thrash thesis missed. Separately, wall_pct as priority rewards big-but-compiler-saturated kernels over small-but-slack ones: the gfx1151 rmsnorm at 0.4% occupancy has low wall_pct yet high headroom, so a wall_pct-only queue ranks it last. (Codex verification errored on this item — treat as asserted-plausible.)
gaps.suggestion: Add and DERIVE-from a latency/stall counter, not just L2-hit: VMEM/VALU issue-stall cycles or an achieved-vs-peak instruction-issue ratio distinguishes latency-bound from ALU-bound within the cache-resident regime (the 'occupancy-starved vs memory-latency-bound' separation occ+mem_busy don't give). Change candidate priority from wall_pct to wall_pct × headroom-estimate, where headroom ≈ (1 − occupancy) or the latency-stall fraction, so under-occupied small kernels — the only place a win was found — surface instead of saturated large ones.

gaps.title: 'Near-tapped ~0%' is partly instrument-limited, and the advancing-baseline per-round margin gate structurally REJECTS the compounding-small-wins regime it then declares empty
gaps.gap: The perf discriminator is end-to-end decode tok/s, whose cross-process noise floor is >=1-3% at fixed clock (wider across processes), and the serve_harness redesign ADDS CLI/HTTP/chatml variance on top. A plausible single-kernel effect on a hot kernel is well under that floor, so 'the loop detects nothing' conflates 'nothing there' with 'nothing resolvable by this instrument.' This interacts fatally with the advancing-baseline margin: set the margin >= noise floor and you reject every real sub-floor win (15 × +0.3% never accumulates because no single step clears the gate); set it < floor and you bank noise (the exact dilution the gate exists to prevent). The cited '15-win within-session stack netted -0.34% fresh-process' is consistent with BOTH 'all illusion' and 'real net-zero + noise' — the instrument cannot distinguish them, yet the strategic conclusion treats it as proof of tapped-out. The live certifiers still bank primarily on decode tok/s (kernel_decode_tok_s/decode_tok_s with f>=0.90); the pinned-clock rocprof duration data is used only as post-verdict BOD feedback, not as the bank gate.
gaps.suggestion: Stop resolving perf on end-to-end tok/s alone. You already collect pinned-clock rocprof kernel DURATION for the BOD — a per-kernel duration delta at profile_standard has far lower variance than auto-clock end-to-end tok/s and directly attributes the change. Use kernel-duration-delta as the PRIMARY perf discriminator (gate on it), with an end-to-end fresh-process run as a magnitude-confirmation only at rollover. This lets the loop bank sub-tok/s-floor kernel wins that genuinely compound, and disambiguates instrument-limited nulls from real nulls before concluding the space is tapped.

gaps.title: Strict monotonic hill-climb plus a permanent 'never re-try a DEAD lever' ban forbids perf-neutral stepping-stone refactors, trapping each card in a local optimum with no valley crossing
gaps.gap: WIN requires strict perf-gain-vs-B_a with margin, and B_a advances only on a WIN, so ab_certify_v2p only commits when f>=0.90 and delta>FLOOR — DEAD/INCONCLUSIVE are logged and discarded, never retained as substrate. A parity-clean, perf-neutral structural refactor (e.g. reorganizing the __shfl-serialized score/V loop so a later register-ring prefetch can attach — the exact shape of the gfx11 +6.95% win, which needed the loop restructured first) is a non-WIN, so B_a is unchanged and the intermediate is discarded. Worse, gen_digest.py:20 instructs Codex to NEVER re-try a lever marked DEAD/INCONCLUSIVE, and update_exhaustion marks that intermediate DEAD — so the stepping-stone lever is permanently banned even though it was the necessary precursor to the compounding win two moves away. Greedy strict-improvement + monotone ban = the classic two-move-win-behind-a-neutral-first-move trap, with no backtracking through banned levers.
gaps.suggestion: Accept parity-clean, coherent, perf-neutral (within-noise) structural variants as LATERAL moves that advance the STRUCTURE of B_a without claiming a perf win (bank them as NEUTRAL, not WIN, so dilution accounting is unaffected but the code substrate advances). Make the DEAD ban lever-SIGNATURE-specific rather than lever-name-specific, and allow a lever to be re-tried when the kernel's structure has changed since it was marked dead. Consider annealed acceptance for the coherence-clean subset only (never accept a regression that ships an attractor).

gaps.title: K=5 conflates INCONCLUSIVE (a small real win buried in noise) with DEAD (no headroom), abandoning exactly the sub-2% regime that is all that's left on the tapped arches — and increments per-attempt, so K can be consumed in ~2 rounds
gaps.gap: update_exhaustion.py increments identically for DEAD and INCONCLUSIVE, and INCONCLUSIVE is defined as the MWU statistic failing to resolve at CAP=16 (0.65<f<0.90) — a real-but-small effect noise didn't let cross the win band, which the review flags as re-openable on rerun. The measurement rules say within-session A/B is optimistic below ~2% and small wins net near-zero on fresh-process, so a genuine +1.5% win is precisely what resolves INCONCLUSIVE. Counting five INCONCLUSIVEs as 'exhausted' declares a kernel dead on five near-wins never confirmed — and the review's own finding is two of three arches are down to sub-percent residuals, so the stop rule is most aggressive exactly where the only remaining wins live. Committed ledgers show 14 INCONCLUSIVE rows all with positive delta (e.g. gfx1201/fused_qkvza_hfq4g256 +1.77%). The counter also increments per-attempt-per-round (a round trying a kernel 3× all-INCONCLUSIVE jumps exh by 3; a gfx1201 R102 round had four same-round failures), so 'K=5 consecutive dead' can be reached in ~2 rounds, not five deliberate attempts.
gaps.suggestion: Split the verdict: INCONCLUSIVE should NOT increment the DEAD streak — route it to a 'needs-confirmation' queue that gets one fresh-process re-measure at higher sample count before WIN/DEAD classification. Make the stop rule expected-value-based: exhaust a kernel when observed win-rate × mean-gain over its attempt history falls below a threshold, not on a raw consecutive-fail count. At minimum cap the per-round increment at 1 so K is genuinely 'consecutive rounds,' not 'attempts.'

gaps.title: Only batch-1 short-context is measured — the operating point that steers the whole loop, the KV-OOB/sliding-window paths, and the named architectural lever (spec-decode/MTP batched verify) are all off-battery, so 'tapped' describes one workload shape
gaps.gap: GENRE_BATTERY is 5 short single-turn prompts; every BOD census and every A/B is batch-1 single-request decode, with no long-context row and no batched-verify mode. The finding 'batch-1 under-saturates BW/CUs, ~6x below BW-peak, latency-bound' is a property of batch-1, NOT of the kernels: at batch>1 (continuous batching) or long-context, GEMV becomes GEMM, FA tiles and KV traffic scale, utilization/BW rise toward peak, and the bound_class flips from latency-shadowed to compute/BW-bound — so traffic-reduction/tiling levers that LOST at batch-1 (register-cliff) can win. For a3b's hottest kernels wall_pct is a strong function of sequence length, so the BOD priority steering the loop is measured at ~500-token context while the engine deploys at 8k-32k. The cohere2moe gate deliberately includes a >4096-token row (sliding-window flash + KV-OOB guard); serve_harness has no equivalent, so those paths are never on the measured surface. And the review's own strategic read says the big remaining levers are architectural (spec-decode/MTP to batch the verify) — inherently batch>1 — which a batch-1-only harness structurally cannot measure. So '2 of 3 arches tapped' is a verdict about one workload shape, not about decode.
gaps.suggestion: Before deciding kernel AR is done, re-census the BOD at batch={4,8} and a >4096-token md5-pinned long-context row, and compare bound_class distributions to batch-1 — if a cluster flips to BW/compute-bound with real occupancy headroom, kernel AR is NOT tapped, it was measured against the wrong workload. Hard-check the KV-capacity/sliding-window paths there. If the loop is to chase the architectural lever, add a batched-verify/spec-decode measurement mode (τ + accepted-token rate through the same serve); otherwise explicitly scope the machine to batch-1 short-context and stop treating 'tapped' as a decode verdict.

gaps.title: The stated higher-leverage pivot (spec-decode / MTP / quant-format) is un-served by the very gate being built — text-exact parity is correct for kernel edits and meaningless for every lever the doc calls more valuable
gaps.gap: The review concludes the big remaining levers are architectural (spec-decode/MTP, quant-format redesign), then the serve_harness design invests all new measurement in ARM A text-exact parity + ARM B attractor coherence. But those levers are NOT value-preserving in the parity sense: spec-decode/MTP change the token stream by construction, and a quant-format redesign changes the output distribution (a KLD question, not a byte-diff). ARM A text-exact parity returns PARITY_FAIL on 100% of these by design, so the gate cannot certify the space it says has headroom. The correct axes are already known-hard in this project's memory: acceptance-rate τ (documented to swing 17% on a single newline; offline proxies REVERSE online) and KLD-vs-a-bf16-oracle (llama.cpp bf16). None of that is in the redesign — the machine is getting better measurement for the search space it declared tapped and no measurement for the one it declared high-leverage.
gaps.suggestion: If the strategic decision is to repoint at architectural levers, spec a THIRD certify axis before building more parity infra: an online τ-acceptance arm (byte-identical committed prompts + md5, per the existing rule) and a KLD/quality arm against the bf16 oracle, with the DFlash three-tier attractor gate already on hand. Decide explicitly whether serve_harness's parity arm is scoped to kernel-edit campaigns only; do not let 'measure everything through parity' block the higher-leverage campaigns.

gaps.title: Attractor detection silently moved from token-ids to whitespace words (reusing token-id thresholds), and the sampling recipe is re-derived in Python instead of read back from the serve — the crutch partly moved rather than being removed
gaps.gap: Two 'reimplemented production behavior can diverge' biases. (1) The DFlash/coherence thresholds (uniq<0.15 first-128, <0.30 last-128, maxfreq>0.50, 3-gram>0.50) were calibrated on TOKEN-IDs (the HIPFIRE_EMIT_TOKEN_IDS committed stream, as coherence-gate-dflash.sh parses). serve_harness has only HTTP text, so it applies the SAME numbers to re.findall(r'\S+') WHITESPACE WORDS (send(), line 241). Words ≠ token-ids: 128 words ≈ 180 tokens, so the 'first-128' window is materially wider (diluting single-token attractors); subword loops inside a word and code's heavy short-token repetition (punctuation the tokenizer splits but whitespace-join fuses) shift both false-negative and false-positive rates unknown-ward. This is an unacknowledged measurement change vs the token-id gate the redesign claims to preserve. (2) resolve_sampling re-implements the production recipe in Python from a filename-inferred tag and a small whitelist, then sends those fields explicitly, while production serve resolves request > registry/per-model > daemon/.hfq/arch defaults (cli/index.ts) including fields the harness doesn't mirror (repeat_penalty, system_prompt) — and the HTTP response returns only usage/timings, not the applied recipe, so the harness cannot prove it measured the same resolved sampling.
gaps.suggestion: For (1): emit token-ids over the HTTP stream (or attach the committed token-id stream) and run the detector on token-ids with the original calibration, OR explicitly re-calibrate the thresholds/window for words and document them as a distinct detector. For (2): have serve_harness ask the running serve what sampling it resolved (echo the applied settings in the response/usage) and assert the harness-resolved recipe byte-matches it, instead of re-deriving from an infer_tag regex + a 5-key whitelist — otherwise 'measure at the production recipe' is unverified.
